intended_object: The isomorphism H^{p,n-p} ≅ H^{n-p,p} between Hodge components of a pure Hodge structure of weight n, given by complex conjugation, viewed as a real-linear isomorphism because conjugation is conjugate-linear. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The forward map sends x ∈ piece p to ω x ∈ piece (n - p); `conj_mem_piece` shows that it lands there. The inverse applies ω again, and `sub_sub_cancel` identifies n - (n - p) with p. The two inverse laws follow from ω being an involution (`ω.apply_apply`). Additivity holds because ω is additive. For real-linearity, conjugation fixes real scalars, so ω(r•x) = conj(r)•ω(x) = r•ω(x). This is exactly the standard fact that conjugation maps H^{p,q} onto H^{q,p}, as the docstring describes.

The definition does not narrow anything. It holds for any complex vector space with any conjugation and for every weight and index. A conjugate-linear equivalence over ℂ (`≃ₗ⋆[ℂ]`) would carry more structure, but the real-linear packaging is a correct statement of the intended object and matches the docstring. Mathlib has no Hodge structures, so it has no counterpart.
